thread:
alex.s: FYI customer (FinexCorp) wants to run a Private deployment POC. Their security team asked for PrivateLink by default but wants an automatic fallback to VPC peering if the interface endpoint saturates. Also sent a security questionnaire. Need quick answers on routing, authz, and minimal firewall rules. cc @priya.se @tom.netops
priya.se: Quick clarifying Qs: 1) Do they require all egress to go through their corporate TLS-inspecting proxy? 2) Do they need client source IPs preserved to upstream models? :eyes:
tom.netops: If they require TLS inspect on customer traffic, they need to terminate TLS at their proxy before it hits our service. PrivateLink is L3/L4 between our ENI and theirs; we don't terminate customer TLS for inspection on their side. For source IP: with interface endpoint the connection shows customer ENI; with hosted NAT we NAT. For Dedicated we can map BYOIP/EIP for SRC preservation in some topologies.
hana.se: Also confirm CIDR they plan to use & region. Pricing signal: PrivateLink itself has no per-connection Redwood surcharge, but egress/throughput and Dedicated capacity are cost drivers. For a POC we can offer credits.
jordan.security: From security side: we can provide boilerplate answers for KMS, audit logs, and flow logs. We don't support forcing customer-side TLS inspection of LLM payloads by default — that's a joint legal/sec discussion. We should provide a recommended configuration that preserves confidentiality while meeting their ask for inspection where applicable.
priya.se: They answered: us-west-2, VPC 10.2.0.0/16, target steady 25 rps (peak 50), ~10k tokens/min. SLA requested 99.9. They want a one-pager for firewall + routing and a snippet for the questionnaire.
tom.netops: Draft allowlist snippet (customer side):
```
# Customer firewall / NSG rules to reach Redwood PrivateLink
allow tcp 443 from 10.2.0.0/16 to <redwood-interface-endpoint-ip>/32  # HTTPS to service endpoint
allow tcp 443 from 10.2.0.0/16 to 169.254.169.254/32  # if using instance metadata for creds (lockdown recommended)
# If using peering fallback, allow return paths for ephemeral ports as needed
allow tcp 1024-65535 from <redwood-subnet-cidr> to 10.2.0.0/16  # for peering traffic return
```
tom.netops: Route guidance: create a specific route for the service endpoint to the interface ENI. For peering fallback, we recommend a canary route that points 10% of traffic to the VPC peering target and 90% to PrivateLink by using our routing proxy-based weighted policy (we will help configure).
hana.se: For the security questionnaire section on encryption + KMS: we support customer-managed KMS for Private deployments (you can bring your CMK). Audit logs: Console exposes token-level ops and model access logs; we can provide retention options and an export to their SIEM. I'll draft language.
priya.se: Pricing notes to include in one-pager: POC (2-week setup + 1 week validation) covered by credits; egress billed at standard rates; Dedicated reserved pricing quoted separately if they want predictable throughput > 100 rps. Need to capture expected sustained tokens/min (they gave 10k) to estimate GPU sizing.
jordan.security: Also request: a short paragraph on data handling during fallbacks (PrivateLink -> Peering). We should explicitly state that when we route over peering we may NAT egress traffic and some SRC IP preservation characteristics change. Customer must accept those differences in the questionnaire.
alex.s: Great. Can we have a one-pager, firewall snippet, and a 2-slide pricing summary by EOD? Sales needs it for the call tomorrow. @hana.se @priya.se please. :thumbsup:
hana.se: On it — I'll include a canary rollout plan (10% -> 50% -> 100%), the firewall snippet above, an ops checklist for route-table changes, and a short note on how to validate :
- health check ping to /healthz
- request-level latency & token metrics
- trace-id mapping for audit logs

deploy-bot: Runbook created: https://redwood-internal/runbooks/privatedeploy-poc-setup (internal link)
priya.se: I'll include a paragraph: 'If customer insists on TLS inspection we recommend they place the proxy before the PrivateLink ENI or use peering where they control the egress path; we will not perform in-line TLS inspection of customer payloads on our hosted endpoints unless contractual & legal approvals are in place.'
alex.s: Excellent. I'll sync with the customer and send the questionnaire bundle once Hana/ Priya upload. Timeline: 24h for docs, 48h to get test endpoint provisioned after signed order.
jordan.security: I'll prepare boilerplate sec answers and flag any high-risk asks.
hana.se: Uploading draft in next 3 hours.
priya.se: tagging pricing to review for Dedicated options.
